transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I just can't seem to shake this feeling that I've ruined things for everyone. I've been really falling behind at work lately, and I've completely lost control of my apartment situation. It just feels like... I don't know, like I deserve whatever bad thing happens to me next.
How long have you been feeling this way—did it start suddenly after a specific event, or has it been building up gradually over months or longer?

It's been... about a year and two months now. It actually started after a specific event. A pipe burst at my old place, which forced me to move into the smaller apartment I'm in now. After that happened, my normal routines just completely fell apart, and I've been feeling this way ever since.
Before this past year and two months, had you ever gone through a period of similar low mood, loss of interest, or hopelessness that lasted for several weeks or more?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had bad days before, like anyone, but... nothing like this. Before the pipe burst, I was doing okay. I went to work, saw friends, kept up with things. This is the first time it's been this bad, for this long.
Over this past year, have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in things you used to enjoy, even when your circumstances weren't reminding you of the apartment situation?

Yeah, I have. Most days I just wake up with this... flat, heavy sadness. It doesn't even have to be about the apartment. It's just there. The things that used to sort of reset me, like putting on a record, cooking a decent meal, or tinkering with my electronics... they just don't reach me anymore. I don't really get anything out of them now.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep over this past year—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?

Yeah, my sleep has been pretty messed up. I'll get into bed, but then I'll just lie there for hours... listening for any noises in the apartment. It takes me forever to drift off. And then, when I finally do, I end up waking up way before dawn. I wake up feeling totally tense and exhausted, almost like my brain never really powered down or got any rest.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight, or found it harder to concentrate on tasks, over this past year?

No, not really. My appetite has been about the same, and I haven't noticed my weight changing at all. And concentrating... I guess that's been fine. I work in IT support, so I have to focus on troubleshooting issues, and I still get my work done without much trouble. So I don't think my focus has been affected.
Have you had any thoughts of wanting to hurt yourself, or thoughts that you'd be better off dead?

I don't have any plan to actually hurt myself, or anything like that. But... I do catch myself thinking sometimes that it would just be easier if I didn't wake up. Like it would be better if I just wasn't around, and nobody had to deal with me anymore. So, yeah, I guess I do have those kinds of thoughts.
Over this past year, have you noticed feeling unusually tired or low on energy, even when you haven't been especially active?

Not really, no. I mean, obviously I feel a bit tired in the mornings because my sleep has been so bad, like I mentioned. But other than that... I wouldn't say I feel unusually drained or low on energy during the day. I still have enough energy to get through my shifts and do what I need to do.
Have other people mentioned noticing that you seem to be moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or conversely, that you seem more restless or fidgety than you used to be?

No one has really said anything to me about it, but... I've noticed it myself, actually. At work, sometimes my hands just hover over the keyboard. It takes me a lot longer to answer even the simple support tickets. It's almost like... like my brain and my body are running on a delayed connection or something. I just feel slower.

Would you say your symptoms have made it nearly impossible to keep up with your usual work and daily responsibilities, or are you still managing to get through most of them, even if it's harder than before?

I'm still managing to get through most of it, but it's definitely harder. I'm still working, but... I've actually had to ask for some accommodations lately. I asked for extra review on my tickets because I keep making these stupid documentation mistakes that I normally wouldn't make. And outside of work... I mean, I still get things done, but I've been skipping some of my regular board-game nights with friends. I just leave the apartment a lot less because keeping up with my normal routine just... it just feels a lot harder than it used to.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a single, first-ever depressive episode of 14 months duration triggered by a psychosocial stressor (pipe burst/relocation), with persistent depressed mood most days, marked anhedonia, sleep disturbance (initial and early morning insomnia), feelings of worthlessness/guilt, psychomotor slowing, and passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent. Appetite, weight, and concentration are unaffected, and energy is only mildly reduced secondary to poor sleep. Functional impairment is present but moderate—he continues working (with accommodations) and maintains most daily responsibilities, though social withdrawal and reduced routine functioning are evident. No prior depressive or manic/hypomanic episodes reported, ruling out recurrent depressive disorder or bipolar spectrum. The combination of core and associated symptoms (≥6 total) with moderate functional impact and no psychotic features fits a single moderate depressive episode (F32.1) rather than mild (F32.0) or severe (F32.2) depression. Adjustment disorder (F43.21) was considered given the clear precipitating stressor, but the pervasive, persistent nature of symptoms independent of the apartment situation, along with sufficient symptom count and duration, meets full criteria for a major depressive episode rather than a stress-reactive adjustment disorder.
